minutes.headline: Personnel Committee voted to recommend a 2.5% COLA for SAP employees, amending down from a proposed 3%.
minutes.summary: The committee debated the COLA for SAP employees effective July 1, 2023. A motion for 3% was amended to 2.5% to match other unions and avoid being cut by the Finance Committee or Select Board. Members also assigned who will present to Finance and the Select Board, and agreed to withhold a consultant payment because the work is late.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee voted to recommend a cost-of-living raise for SAP employees at 2.5%, amended down from a proposed 3%, effective July 1, 2023.
The original motion for a 3% raise was made first; the vote count on it and on the amendment is not audible in the recording.
Members agreed to hold the final consultant payment until the deliverables are met, because the work ran past its deadline.
Members were assigned to present to the Finance Committee and the Select Board, and a total dollar impact of the raise is to be prepared for them.
The next meeting is set for April 12 with the consultant.

why_it_matters: The recommended SAP raise goes to the Finance Committee and the Select Board, whose decisions set the town payroll line that taxes fund.
The raise was set ahead of the compensation study, so it applies before the study's findings are known.
watch_next: The Finance Committee and Select Board presentations, including the Select Board on Tuesday, April 4, where the total dollar impact of the raise is to be shown.
The April 12 meeting with the consultant, and whether the final payment is released.

reconciliation.summary:
The two records agree on the shape of the meeting: a 3% COLA motion amended to 2.5%, the consultant payment withheld, and the next meeting on April 12. Ours is thinner on names and the official is thinner on discussion.
The thing to check is the vote: the official says the 2.5% amendment passed, our recording has the outcome inaudible, and neither shows a vote on the main motion as amended. The scheduling of the presentations also reads differently.
